Q1: Calcium hypochlorite exhibits known GHS-classified hazards (Tier 1) for environmental, inhalation, oral, dermal and eye, and organ and systemic hazards. However, its carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR) and endocrine disruption hazards (EDC) are currently classified as data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Calcium hypochlorite is listed as a hazardous substance under the Clean Water Act, indicating it poses an imminent and substantial danger to public health or welfare if discharged into navigable waters. It is not identified on any lists that designate it as a low-hazard chemical.
Q3: Calcium hypochlorite is extensively characterized, with 6,174 chemical literature references, well above the median for the specialized chemical dataset. Its molecular formula and substance class are clearly defined, and it is not classified as a UVCB, further indicating a well-understood identity. Although a few hazard classes are data deficient, the substantial body of literature suggests a comprehensive understanding of its properties.
